screen.summary: The root of one complete interface: a page, a view or an app screen.
screen.guidance: Every document has exactly one screen. State in `purpose` what the person using it is trying to get done; renderers and design rules read it.

name.description: Stable, kebab-case identifier for the screen.

purpose.description: One sentence describing what the user accomplishes on this screen.

section.summary: A region of the screen that groups content serving one goal.
section.guidance: Sections may be nested. Heading levels are derived from section depth, so authors never choose a heading level by hand.

name.description: Stable, kebab-case identifier for the section. Unique within the screen.

emphasis.description: How strongly the section should stand out from its siblings.

heading.summary: The title of the section that contains it.
heading.guidance: Its level comes from the section depth. Use at most one heading per section.

text.summary: A paragraph of explanatory or supporting copy.
text.guidance: Use `tone="muted"` for secondary copy such as notes and fine print.

field.summary: A single input that collects one value from the user.
field.guidance: Every field needs a visible `label`. Use `unit` for measured values (for example `kg` or `m`) instead of writing the unit into the label.

name.description: Stable identifier for the submitted value. Unique within the screen.

label.description: Visible label that names the value.

kind.description: The kind of value collected, which selects the input control.

required.description: Whether a value must be provided.

hint.description: Short help text shown with the field.

unit.description: Unit of measurement for the value, such as `kg`, `mm` or `PKR`.

action.summary: Something the user can do: submit, navigate, reset, cancel or delete.
action.guidance: Describe what happens with `intent` and how important it is with `importance`; never describe how it looks. Its text content is the accessible label.

intent.description: What happens when the action is taken.

importance.description: How important the action is relative to others in the same section.

target.description: Destination of a `navigate` action, such as a path or screen name.

feedback.summary: A message that reports a result, status or problem to the user.
feedback.guidance: Pick `tone` by meaning, not by colour. Renderers announce feedback to assistive technology.
